note: Researcher-developed assessment catalogue for an academic prototype. It is not an official control set of the CBN, NIST, ISO or ISACA. Questions, evidence lists, weights and targets are the researcher's own wording and design choices.

App III 1.5.text: Minimum security baseline configuration and hardening

App III 1.6(g).text: Regular data backup, secure backup storage, and regular testing of restoration

App III 2.1(d).text: Monitoring of the physical environment, including the disaster recovery site

App III 2.1(e).text: Security monitoring through a security operations centre

App III 2.1(g).text: Logging enabled on all systems and applications

controls.title: Board and CISO accountability for cyber resilience
controls.question: Has the Board assigned responsibility for the cybersecurity and resilience programme, and is a CISO in post with the reporting line the CBN requires?
evidence: Board or committee terms of reference
controls.rationale: All sources place accountability with leadership. The CBN text is the most specific for Nigerian banks, so it is the primary anchor.
controls.remediation: Confirm Board-level ownership of the programme and a CISO appointment that meets the CBN requirements.

controls.title: Board-approved risk appetite and acceptance criteria
controls.question: Are risk appetite and risk acceptance criteria approved by the Board and used when a resilience gap is accepted instead of fixed?
evidence: Example of an acceptance decision recorded against the criteria
controls.rationale: Decision rules DR3 and DR10 allow a gap to be accepted only under approved criteria, so the criteria must exist first.
controls.remediation: Obtain Board approval of acceptance criteria and apply them to every recorded exception.

controls.title: Reporting of recovery exercise results and open exceptions
controls.question: Do senior management and the Board receive the results of recovery exercises and the list of open resilience exceptions?
evidence: Board or committee report showing exercise outcomes
Exception register extract presented to management
controls.rationale: The CBN requires drill outcomes to reach senior management and quarterly Board reports. Reporting open exceptions alongside them is this study's addition.
controls.remediation: Add exercise outcomes and open exceptions to the regular management and Board reports.

controls.title: Inventory of assets supporting the service
controls.question: Is there a current inventory of the assets that deliver this service, each with a named owner?
evidence: Asset inventory extract for the service
controls.rationale: Every source requires an asset inventory. Tying it to a service is what makes it usable for recovery planning.
controls.remediation: Complete the asset inventory for the service and assign an owner to each asset.

controls.title: Criticality classification of the service and its assets
controls.question: Has the service been classified for criticality, with its critical assets identified?
evidence: Criticality rating and the reason for it
controls.rationale: The CBN definition of critical systems supplies the test in DR1. CSF ID.AM-05 states the same outcome.
controls.remediation: Classify the service and its assets using the DR1 criterion and record the result.

controls.title: Dependency map for the service
controls.question: Are the shared components, network connections and third-party connections this service depends on mapped and reviewed?
evidence: Catalogue of third-party connections with date of last review
controls.rationale: The CBN requires a topology diagram and a catalogue of third-party connections. Organising them per service is this study's addition (Finding Two).
controls.remediation: Map every shared and external dependency of the service and review the map after significant change.

controls.title: Multi-factor authentication on critical systems
controls.question: Do the critical systems of this service require multi-factor authentication?
evidence: List of systems covered and any exclusions
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement for critical systems, matched by CSF and ISO.
controls.remediation: Enforce multi-factor authentication on every critical system of the service.

controls.title: Privileged and service accounts recorded and reviewed
controls.question: Are privileged and service accounts with access to the production or recovery environment of this service recorded in an access control matrix and reviewed?
evidence: Record of the latest review and the changes made
controls.rationale: Condition (a) of DR4. The CBN access control matrix is the primary anchor.
controls.remediation: Record all privileged and service accounts for the service in the access control matrix and review them.

controls.title: Recovery administration separated from production
controls.question: Is the recovery environment administered with credentials and tools that are not shared with production?
evidence: List of recovery administration accounts and tools
Check showing production credentials do not work in the recovery environment
Any recorded exception with its compensating control
controls.rationale: Condition (b) of DR4, from Findings Three and Five. No CBN requirement was identified in the text read; CSF PR.AA-05 covers separation of duties in general terms only.
controls.remediation: Give the recovery environment its own administrative credentials and tools, or record an exception with a compensating control.

controls.title: Vendor access approved, limited, time-bound and monitored
controls.question: Is vendor access to the systems of this service approved, limited in scope and duration, monitored and revoked after use?
evidence: Evidence of revocation after the task
controls.rationale: Condition (c) of DR4. A direct CBN requirement.
controls.remediation: Put vendor access under approval, scope and time limits, monitoring and revocation.

controls.title: Network segmentation around the service
controls.question: Are the production, recovery, user and third-party network zones of this service separated, with only documented connections allowed between them?
evidence: List of approved connections between zones
controls.rationale: Segmentation is recommended by CISA et al. (2023) and ISO. The CBN text read requires a topology diagram and connection catalogue but states no explicit segmentation requirement, so the basis is Std, not Reg.
controls.remediation: Separate the service's network zones and allow only documented connections between them.

controls.title: Segmentation tested in both directions
controls.question: Has a test shown both that an unauthorised path into the service is blocked and that normal transactions still pass?
evidence: Test script and result for the blocked path
Test result for the normal transaction
controls.rationale: From Finding Five: a restriction that blocks legitimate transactions is also a failure. The paired test is this study's proposal; the CBN penetration test requirement is related but not equivalent.
controls.remediation: Run and record a paired test: blocked unauthorised access and an unaffected normal transaction.

controls.title: Alternative capacity for critical components
controls.question: Does each critical component of this service have an alternative, so that no single point of failure is left untreated?
evidence: List of single points of failure and their treatment
controls.rationale: ISO and CSF address redundancy directly. The CBN text read addresses single points of failure in the industry, not inside a bank, so it is a related reference only.
controls.remediation: Provide an alternative for each critical component or record the treatment of the single point of failure.

controls.title: Fail-over demonstrated by test
controls.question: Has fail-over to the alternative been tested successfully within the validity period?
evidence: Fail-over test report with date and result
Comparison of achieved time against the approved RTO
controls.rationale: Finding Four: an alternative that has not been exercised is unproven.
controls.remediation: Test fail-over and record the result against the approved recovery time objective.

controls.title: Alternative is independent of the compromise
controls.question: Would the alternative remain trustworthy if the primary were compromised, for example by unwanted changes replicating or by a shared administrative element?
evidence: Analysis of what the primary and the alternative share
Replication design showing how corrupted data is prevented from propagating unchecked
controls.rationale: Finding Three, drawing on Ross et al. (2021). No reviewed source states it as a testable requirement.
controls.remediation: Identify what the primary and the alternative share and remove or control each shared element.

controls.title: Protected backup copy
controls.question: Is a backup of this service's data held in a copy that production administrators cannot alter or delete?
evidence: Access list for the protected copy
Configuration showing offline or immutable storage
controls.rationale: Condition (a) of DR5. The CBN requires secure backup storage; CISA et al. (2023) recommend offline copies; protection from production administrators is this study's criterion.
controls.remediation: Hold a backup copy that production administrators cannot alter or delete.

controls.title: Restoration tested within the validity period
controls.question: Has restoration of this service's data from backup been tested successfully within the validity period?
evidence: Restoration test report with date and result
Data set restored and time taken
controls.rationale: Condition (b) of DR5. A direct CBN requirement; the validity period is set by the bank.
controls.remediation: Run a restoration test for the service's data and record the date and result.

controls.title: Clean recovery point identified
controls.question: Is the recovery point checked for integrity and for indicators of compromise, and is the clean recovery point identified and recorded?
evidence: Scan result for indicators of compromise
Record naming the clean recovery point
controls.rationale: Condition (c) of DR5. CSF RC.RP-03 states the outcome; the CBN verify-before-restore requirement concerns the threat, not the data, so it is related only.
controls.remediation: Check recovery points for integrity and compromise and record which one is clean.

controls.title: Logging on systems supporting the service
controls.question: Is logging enabled on the systems of this service, including the activity of privileged users?
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement, matched by CSF and ISO.
controls.remediation: Enable logging, including privileged activity, on every system of the service.

controls.title: Continuous monitoring covers production and recovery
controls.question: Does continuous monitoring through a security operations centre cover this service's systems in both the production and the recovery environment?
evidence: Evidence that recovery-environment sources are onboarded
controls.rationale: The CBN requires 24x7 monitoring through a SOC. Asking explicitly about the recovery environment is this study's addition.
controls.remediation: Extend monitoring coverage to every system of the service, including the recovery environment.

controls.title: Incident response plan with criteria for moving to recovery
controls.question: Does an incident response plan or playbook cover this service and state that threats must be verified as addressed before systems, data or access are restored?
evidence: Incident response plan or playbook for the service
The section stating the criteria for moving to recovery
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement and the documentary basis of DR7.
controls.remediation: Write or update the playbook for the service and include the verify-before-restore criteria.

controls.title: Notification workflow documented
controls.question: Is there a documented workflow for the external notifications an incident affecting this service may require, with triggers, recipients and time limits?
evidence: Named role responsible for each notification
controls.rationale: The CBN 24-hour duty is read from the framework text. The data protection and national CERT duties are taken from Table 1.1 of the paper and were not re-read here. Combining them into one workflow is this study's proposal.
controls.remediation: Document the notification workflow with triggers, recipients, time limits and owners.

controls.title: Incident response exercised
controls.question: Has incident response for this service been exercised by a drill or tabletop within the validity period, with the outcome reported to senior management?
evidence: Record of the report to senior management
Changes made to the plan afterwards
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement.
controls.remediation: Run a drill or tabletop exercise for the service and report the outcome to senior management.

controls.title: Approved recovery requirements from business impact analysis
controls.question: Are the maximum tolerable downtime, RTO and RPO for this service derived from a business impact analysis and approved in writing by the business owner and the risk function?
evidence: Business impact analysis for the service
Written approval of the recovery requirements
controls.rationale: DR2. The CBN text read does not mention recovery time or recovery point objectives, so the basis is NIST SP 800-34 and ISO 22301; the approval roles are this study's proposal.
controls.remediation: Complete the business impact analysis and obtain written approval of the recovery requirements.

controls.title: Service recovery plan documented
controls.question: Is there a documented recovery plan for this service, including coordination with its providers?
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement and a condition of DR6.
controls.remediation: Document the recovery plan for the service, including provider coordination.

controls.title: Service-level restoration exercise completed
controls.question: Has a restoration exercise for the whole service, not only its systems, been completed within the validity period and its outcome reported to senior management?
evidence: Exercise report with date, scope and result
Record of the report to senior management
controls.rationale: A condition of DR6. The CBN requires drills and recovery testing; requiring the exercise at the level of the whole service is this study's criterion (Finding Four).
controls.remediation: Run a restoration exercise for the whole service and report the outcome.

controls.title: Transaction reconciliation as a condition of resumption
controls.question: Is there a defined procedure to reconcile this service's transactions after restoration, and is its completion a condition of resuming the service?
controls.rationale: DR8 and DR9, from Finding Four. No reviewed source specifies service-level reconciliation checks. CSF RC.RP-05 covers the integrity of restored assets in general terms.
controls.remediation: Define the reconciliation procedure and make its completion a condition of resumption.

controls.title: Register of providers and connections for the service
controls.question: Is there a current record of the third-party providers and connections this service relies on, with their criticality?
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement, matched by CSF GV.SC-04.
controls.remediation: Record every provider and connection the service relies on and rate its criticality.

controls.title: Provider contracts and periodic assessment
controls.question: Do contracts with this service's critical providers include security and recovery obligations and a right to audit, and are the providers assessed periodically?
evidence: Latest provider assessment or audit report
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement, matched by CSF and ISO.
controls.remediation: Add security, recovery and audit clauses to provider contracts and assess providers periodically.

controls.title: Recovery coordination tested with critical providers
controls.question: Has recovery been tested jointly with this service's critical providers within the validity period?
evidence: Joint exercise report with date and result
controls.rationale: A direct CBN requirement. It also feeds the DR3 test for an unresolved provider dependency.
controls.remediation: Run a joint recovery test with each critical provider and record the result.
